newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Britain urges Bulgaria to unravel "umbrella murder".
newsitem.headline: Britain urges Bulgaria to unravel "umbrella murder".

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind appealed to Bulgaria's new president on Tuesday to solve the so-called "umbrella murder" of dissident Georgi Markov in London 19 years ago.

"We hope that after the next elections when a new Bulgarian government is in office they will themselves see this is an important priority," Rifkind told reporters after meeting President Petar Stoyanov.
Bulgaria, hit by mass street protests, is in a political deadlock which Stoyanov sought to resolve on Tuesday by asking the ruling Socialists, composed largely of ex-communists to form a government.
The opposition insists on holding elections in March, but the Socialists want to hold them at the end of the year at the earliest.
Rifkind arrived in Bulgaria on Tuesday for talks with Stoyanov and acting foreign minister Irina Bokova. He is due to leave for Rome early on Wednesday.

Stoyanov, who took office last week, said: "I have no sufficient powers to unravel the case on my own, but the Markov murder is one of the ugliest pages in Bulgarian history...I will do my best to shed more light on it so it no longer casts a shadow over our bilateral relations."
Markov was an outspoken critic of Bulgaria's former communist regime and worked for the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) World Service's Bulgarian section.
He died after feeling a sharp jab in the leg as he waited for a bus on Waterloo Bridge in central London.
A poisoned pellet later found in his thigh was assumed to have come from the tip of an umbrella.
Bulgarian officials have said they believed the communist regime which collapsed in 1989 carried out the killing with help from Moscow.
In 1991 a Bulgarian general was sentenced to 14 months in prison for destroying secret files on the case, but officials have not revealed any evidence.
